dish: Michelin-listed ketchup-forward bak chor mee (from S$3)
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-39, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: A Michelin Guide-listed old-school minced meat noodle at 724 AMK Central — springy mee pok or mee kia tossed in a distinctive ketchup-forward chilli sauce with minced pork, braised mushroom and a round cracker, from S$3. Loaded portions and one of the heartland's most-cited bak chor mee stalls.

dish: Wet fried Hokkien prawn mee in wild-prawn stock
n: Eng Ho Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee
address: 409 AMK Market & Food Centre (Teck Ghee Square), #01-34, Blk 409 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560409
w: A wetter, prawn-stock-drenched fried Hokkien mee at 409 (Teck Ghee Square) built on a rich stock of wild sea prawns (swa lor), squid and pork for a sweeter, more delicate depth. Fried in batches with 30-40 minute peak-hour waits; named a top-10 Hokkien mee in Singapore by Lianhe Wanbao. Opens 4pm, closed alternate Tuesdays.

dish: Pork-ribs prawn noodle simmered with black sugarcane
n: Zhen Ming Pork Ribs Prawn Noodle
address: Mayflower Market & Food Centre, #01-04, Blk 162 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560162
w: A 20-plus-year Mayflower stall whose brown prawn broth is simmered at least six hours with pork ribs, pig skin, red dates, prawn shells and black sugarcane (in place of rock sugar) for a natural, addictive sweetness — served dry or soup with fishcake, lean meat, Brazilian pork ribs and prawns. Mornings only; closed Tuesdays.

dish: Johor-style bi tai mak in a gravy-thick pork broth
address: Kebun Baru Market & Food Centre, Blk 226H Ang Mo Kio Street 22, S560226 (stall no. to confirm)
w: A perpetual pre-lunch queue at Kebun Baru since Dec 2020 for a Johor-Bahru-style bi tai mak (S$4) rarely found this side of the Causeway — freshly-made 'rat-tail' noodles in a viscous, gravy-like broth crossing robust pork stock with light ikan bilis, studded with minced pork, mushroom, hae bee, garlic, fried shallots and salted fish. Sells out before lunch.

A 24-hour Jalan Kayu institution on the AMK/Seletar fringe serving Singaporean, Malay, Thai and South Indian fare — famed for its prata, biryani, satay and curry fish head, with an air-conditioned wing alongside the coffeeshop seating. Packed at breakfast and supper.

dish: Wet wok-hei char kway teow with S$1 otah
address: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-32, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
w: A Sembawang Hills favourite (formerly at Shunfu/Lakeview) for a wet, wok-hei char kway teow with cockles, beansprouts and Chinese sausage from S$3, best paired with its smoky S$1 otah. Closed Mondays.

dish: Muslim-owned handmade dim sum from S$2.50
address: Blk 260 Ang Mo Kio Street 21, S560260
w: A Muslim-owned dim sum stall (sharing a coffeeshop with Friends Kitchen HK, whose team co-owns it) doing an unusually wide handmade range from S$2.50 — chunky chicken-and-shrimp siew mai, fluffy BBQ chicken buns and salted-egg lava buns — a genuine rarity as halal dim sum in the heartland.

dish: Nanyang-style mani cai mee hoon kueh & kopi under S$8
address: Blk 163 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, #01-414, S560163
w: A 2025-opened old-school Nanyang cafe doing classic heartland fare — mani cai (sayur manis) mee hoon kueh, laksa, steamed toast and frothy kopi, most mains under S$8, CDC vouchers accepted. Open daily 7am-10pm.

dish: Mahjong-themed gelato, croffles & nian gao waffles
address: Blk 128 Ang Mo Kio Ave 3, #01-1867, S560128
w: A void-deck gelato cafe themed around mahjong — flavours inspired by Chinese sweets, served with Belgian waffles, croffles and pandan-mochi or nian gao waffles, the tiles motif carried playfully through the shop. Open till late on weekends.

dish: Home-style mee soto, mee rebus, lontong & nasi lemak
address: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-97, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
w: A home-style Malay stall at 628 turning out comforting mee soto, mee rebus, lontong and nasi lemak — a neighbourhood staple recommended in both Seth Lui's and Eatbook's 628 round-ups.

dish: Vegetarian bee hoon & meat-free zi char
address: Ang Mo Kio 628 Market & Food Centre, #01-70, Blk 628 Ang Mo Kio Ave 4, S560628
w: A 628 vegetarian stall doing curry vegetarian bee hoon in the morning and, from mid-afternoon, meat-free zi char — mock duck rice, fish-soup bee hoon and stir-fried sweet potato leaves — a rare all-vegetarian option in the centre.

address: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-27, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
w: A long-loved, no-frills braised duck rice and porridge counter at Sembawang Hills, a Thomson-and-Sembawang neighbourhood standby featured across the centre's guides.

dish: Rich, gooey mee rebus, mee siam, lontong & nasi lemak
address: Sembawang Hills Food Centre, #01-17, 590 Upper Thomson Road, S574419
w: A Muslim-owned, halal-certified stall at Sembawang Hills known for a rich, gooey mee rebus alongside mee siam, lontong and nasi lemak — homely Malay breakfast fare in a mostly-Chinese food centre.

dish: Fishball kway teow soup with in-house chilli
n: Xiang Kee Yu Yuan Mian Tang
address: Cheng San Market & Cooked Food Centre, #01-125, Blk 527 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, S560527
w: A husband-and-wife fishball noodle stall of some 30 years at Cheng San — a lardy, savoury-tangy fishball kway teow soup (from S$4) with minced meat, mushroom, pork lard and fresh liver, its in-house chilli of dried chillies and shallots giving a fiery kick. Queues form from 7am; closed Mondays.

dish: Old-school hawker Western grills since the 1990s
address: Ang Mo Kio Central Market & Food Centre, #01-08, Blk 724 Ang Mo Kio Ave 6, S560724
w: A 724 AMK Central Western stall going since the 1990s, a longstanding heartland pick for grilled and deep-fried meats — chicken, pork chop and steak — in the old-school Hainanese-Western tradition. Opens afternoons, closed Mondays.

dish: Mochi pancakes & waffles with gelato at nett prices
address: Blk 446 Ang Mo Kio Ave 10, #01-1661, S560446
w: An under-HDB dessert cafe doing chewy mochi pancakes, mochi waffles and gelato at nett prices (from S$4.50), open late on weekends — a 14-minute walk from AMK MRT. (Status to re-verify: one report suggests the unit has since changed hands.)
